sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Administration of Employee Share Incentive Plans (ESOP Trusts)

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (single unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax or registration autonomy)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition, French Napoleonic lineage; unitary national legal system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 on the Abolition of the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention)

Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and Capital (signed 12 March 1985, as amended by the Protocol of 20 January 2009)

Agreement between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and Capital Gains (1995, as amended by the 2010 Protocol)

Treaty of Friendship, Establishment and Navigation between the United States of America and Luxembourg (signed 23 February 1962) and the Luxembourg-United States DTA (1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), including the free movement of capital and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) framework

Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes between States and Nationals of Other States (ICSID) and the Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (BEPS MLI), both ratified by Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme (2004 AML/CFT Law), as subsequently amended and consolidated; CSSF Regulation N°12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners, the 'RBE Law'), as subsequently amended; Loi du 19 décembre 2002 sur le registre du commerce et des sociétés (Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies); Loi du 31 mai 1999 sur la domiciliation des sociétés (Law of 31 May 1999 on company domiciliation); EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 as transposed; EU Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (competent authorities and AML/CFT obliged entities hold direct statutory access; the general public may obtain extracts only upon demonstrating a legitimate interest, subject to the RBE Law and the Luxembourg data-protection regime)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial instrument of incorporation of the SCSp (acte constitutif and articles of partnership)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary public (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg); if executed abroad, the signatures are legalized by the competent Luxembourg consulate or under apostille prior to filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (only if the deed is notarized outside Luxembourg and is to be used in another Hague Contracting State; domestic Luxembourg filings are self-authenticating)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Legalizations Service of the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs for foreign use; non-Hague destination requiring Consular Legalization through the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the destination state's consular mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of name availability / certificate of non-immatriculation (certificat de non-immatriculation) for pre-incorporation name clearance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille when the certificate is presented to foreign registries or banks; internal LBR validation for the domestic filing is electronic and does not require legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Excerpt from the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE extract / relevé des bénéficiaires effectifs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) upon conclusion of the post-incorporation UBO declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign regulatory presentation; direct digital access by Luxembourg AML obliged entities and competent authorities is non-legitimized

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners at or above the 25% UBO threshold, authorized representatives, and other officers against the consolidated EU sanctions lists (Council Regulation (EU) No 1945/2011 as amended and EU autonomous asset-freeze lists under Council Decision 2011/172/CFSP), the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the Luxembourg CSSF AML/CFT circular guidance, the FATF black-and-grey lists, OFAC SDN and sectoral lists where US-dollar clearing or US securities are involved, and the domestic sanctions implementation of the Grand-Duchy; Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), family members and close associates trigger mandatory Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the 2004 AML Law, requiring source-of-wealth documentation, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring; the compliance file must evidence a documented risk-based approach, negative-list screening results, and a written UBO affidavit prepared by external legal counsel.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - eRCS online filing platform (www.lbr.lu), operated pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002, integrated with the Guichet.lu single administrative window
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCS register is administered in the French, German and Luxembourgish languages; all filings and publications must be made in at least one of these languages, with certified translations into French or German required for deeds drafted in other languages. The company name may be expressed in a foreign language provided it is registered in Latin-script transliteration and is capable of being read and pronounced locally. The name of an SCSp must be truthful, distinctive within the RCS index, not contrary to public policy or morality, and must not mislead as to the nature or size of the partnership. The corporate denomination of an SCSp must include the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' in the formal name or in the registered corporate identifier; references to 'trust', 'limited partnership' or similar foreign-equivalent terms are permitted only where the statutory form of the SCSp is accurately disclosed, so as to avoid confusion with an incorporated trust or a company with separate legal personality.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Crédit (requires CSSF banking licence)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (requires Commissariat aux Assurances licence)
Fonds / Fund / Investment Fund / OPCM (requires CSSF registration or notification under Part II of the Law of 17 December 2010)
Établissement de crédit / Credit institution / Paiement / Payment institution
Société Nationale / National / État / State patronage implying royal or governmental sponsorship
Luxembourg / Grand-Ducal (requires prior ministerial or Grand-Ducal authorization)
Portefeuille / Holding / Patrimoine (sensitive to tax-substance review and requires accurate business-object description)
ESOP / Employee Benefit Trust (protective wording must not imply a legalpersonality trust; must be framed as an administrative mandate of an SCSp)
Police / Gendarmerie / Militaire / Authority-like tokens (reserved for public bodies)
EU / Union Européenne / European or United Nations identifiers (protected emblems)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a statutory pre-incorporation name-reservation register; the LBR electronic pre-validation and the certificate of non-immatriculation secure a de facto availability window of approximately 30 calendar days. Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) re-file the same name through the eRCS portal with supplementary arguments demonstrating distinctiveness, (ii) file a modified name that remediates the registrar's objection without incurring further fees beyond the standard LBR tariff, or (iii) request a formal written refusal decision from the LBR registrar and, within three months, lodge an administrative appeal before the Tribunal administratif (Administrative Court) pursuant to the general administrative-procedure law and the Law of 19 December 2002; contentious refusal to register after incorporation falls under the competence of the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg. In practice, the fastest corrective path is a revised name filing, while a judicial appeal is reserved for cases involving rights of third parties or reputational necessity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The SCSp must have its registered office (siège social) in Luxembourg and must maintain genuine local substance under the Law of 31 May 1999 on company domiciliation and CSSF professional-domestication standards. The services of a licensed professional domiciliation agent may be used for the statutory seat address, but for the present ESOP-administration business the SCSp must demonstrate real economic substance: decision-making and central administration in Luxembourg, local books and records, accessible officers or delegates, and adequate governance. A purely virtual mailbox without personnel or administrative substance is unacceptable for this industry and would fail the AML/CFT supervision test and the substance expectations of the Luxembourg tax administration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-elevated quantified risk of 20-30% within the first financial period: the CSSF, the Luxembourg tax administration (Administration des contributions directes), and the RBE supervisory authorities conduct risk-based unannounced inspections targeting fiduciary vehicles, pass-through partnerships administering employee equity programmes, and registered-office agents; such inspections are authorized under the 2004 AML/CFT Law and CSSF Regulation 12-02, and the low-risk rating of the banking tier does not eliminate inspection exposure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registry incorporation filing fee - RCS registration of the constitutive instrument with electronic publication (eRCS/RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the LBR fee schedule pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 (EUR 75-85 per filing; USD converted at 1.08)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability pre-validation and certificate of non-immatriculation (certificat de non-immatriculation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR certificate tariff (approximately EUR 55; USD converted at 1.08)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) - electronic initial beneficial-ownership declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee for the initial electronic RBE declaration (free-of-charge LBR e-filing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed drafting, substantive review and execution before a Luxembourg notary (acte constitutif of the SCSp)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark and notarial tariff bracket for a partnership deed (EUR 2,200-3,200 excluding VAT, scaled to transaction complexity)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization service (bundle of four corporate originals processed through the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Legalizations Service (Service des législations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document apostille fee of approximately EUR 14-18 plus official handling charge (estimate for four documents; USD converted at 1.08)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of constitutive documents into French or German (for originals drafted in English or another non-administrative language)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) approved by the Luxembourg District Court or the Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for certified translation (EUR 0.18-0.28 per word combined with statutory per-page notarization of translator's signature)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and professional domiciliation service for the first fiscal year (Law of 31 May 1999 compliance, legal mail handling and corporate-file custody)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized professional domiciliation agent (registered with the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice or a licensed financial-sector professional)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for SCSp domiciliation services (EUR 1,500-2,500 per annum inclusive of standard corporate-administration duties)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External AML/CFT and UBO-piercing compliance mandate (identity verification, PEP and sanctions screening, UBO affidavit drafting and source-of-funds documentation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent Luxembourg law firm or AML compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Blended market rate of EUR 250-450 per hour or fixed fee of EUR 1,200-1,800 per UBO/KYC mandate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Chapter on Special Limited Partnerships (société en commandite spéciale) introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013, and related registral provisions under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the commercial register
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de société / partnership agreement and electronic inscription declaration to the RCS, followed by mandatory publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-up capital is required for a Luxembourg SCSp; the SCSp has no legal personality, and contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement. Contributions may be in cash, in kind, or industry. No statutory escrow account is required for a non-regulated SCSp; as an ESOP administration vehicle, it is not subject to CSSF capitalization rules unless separately regulated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of [General Partner S.à r.l.], acting as general partner of the Luxembourg SCSp under formation, approves the execution of the initial partnership agreement and the subscription of partnership interests in the Special Limited Partnership for the exclusive purpose of administering employee share incentive plans. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp be established at [address] in Luxembourg. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed manager and authorized signatory of the general partner for formation filings. FURTHER RESOLVED, that partners’ cash and in-kind contributions be accepted according to the capital schedule, and that officers be authorized to complete RCS registration and related formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – online company search and pre-filing inquiry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name-conflict and reserved-name search through the RCS electronic database. Confirm that the proposed SCSp name distinguishes the partnership from existing entities and complies with Luxembourg public-order naming rules. Submit any optional name-reservation request or proceed directly to drafting the partnership agreement with the selected name.
required_dossiers: Proposed SCSp name
Identification documents of all initial partners and the general partner
Draft partnership agreement indicating the registered name
Power of attorney if formation is filed by a statutory agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or marked confusing, promptly file an alternative name through the RCS pre-filing channel or submit a reasoned correction request; administrative refusal may be appealed before the competent civil court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional) or general partner under private signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a tailor-made contrât de société governing the SCSp: name, registered office, purpose (administration of employee stock ownership trusts), general partner details, limited partner identity and contribution schedule, capital and profit-sharing provisions, management powers, transfer rules, and dissolution terms. Execute the agreement by all partners either in private writing or by notarial deed if immovable property is contributed.
required_dossiers: Final partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Identity evidence / certificate of non-condemnation for the authorised representative
Capital contribution schedule
Express consent to the purpose limited to ESOP administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the clauses, rectification is made by supplementary agreement or notarial deed; ambiguous capital or purpose clauses are clarified and re-executed before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local commune registration and landlord / property owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enter into a registered-office agreement or lease with a physical address in Luxembourg. Obtain the written consent of the owner for use as the registered office and, where required, register the occupancy with the local commune. Ensure that the office address is active and capable of receiving legal process.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or sublease agreement
Owner's written consent to registration
Extract of property title or official cadastral reference where needed
Proof of address availability letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the landlord consent is not sufficient or the address is rejected, obtain an alternative compliant Luxembourg address and amend the draft partnership agreement before RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File formation and register with RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS e-filing portal (myguichet.lu professional eDesk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic inscription declaration together with the executed partnership agreement, proof of registered office, identification of the general partner, and authorisations. Pay the applicable filing fee and request publication of the formation notice in RESA. The RCS registrar checks compliance and issues the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Completed RCS inscription declaration
Executed partnership agreement
Proof of registered office and owner consent
Identification of general partner, managers and authorised signatories
Power of attorney for e-filing representative
Publication request for RESA entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, correct the identified deficiencies and resubmit through the RCS e-filing portal within the stated deadline; an aggrieved applicant may appeal the registrar's refusal before the tribunal de paix in Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the official RCS extract and registration number. Register the SCSp / general partner with the AEDT if VATable income is anticipated and confirm optional deduction at source. Open the SCSp's dedicated bank account; file any deemed appointment declarations and update the partnership ledger with partner registers and minute book.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate / extract
Partnership agreement and capital contribution records
VAT registration form (if applicable)
Bank account opening pack and beneficial-owner declaration
Partner and manager appointment register and minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of delayed post-registration documents, follow up with the competent administrations by referencing the RCS number and, if necessary, apply for administrative correction or judicial review before the competent administrative court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – Luxembourg does not subject employee stock ownership trust administration or office-based ESOP administration to a physical industrial licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating licence required for the SCSp itself; general partner remains subject to ordinary company-law duties only.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based administrative activity with no classified installation under Luxembourg environmental legislation; no full EIA report or registration threshold is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the ESOP administrative activity; no wastewater, VOC, or industrial waste streams are generated. If an ordinary office lease exists, only municipal sewer use and standard heating, ventilation and air-conditioning emissions thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Standard workplace fire-safety and occupational-health clearance applies under the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and the Corps grand-ducal d’incendie et de secours (CGDIS); a simple office floor plan, fire-extinguisher verification, and emergency-exit certification are sufficient. No special structural-load inspection or industrial risk clearance is required because the SCSp has no manufacturing or physical production activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration, with e-filing via the MyGuichet.lu portal (guichet.lu); indirect taxation is governed by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Luxembourg VAT Authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities acquiring a Luxembourg presence must first obtain a statutory matricule (tax identification number) from the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) at incorporation or registration; this matricule serves as the TIN in relations with the ACD. For VAT purposes, an EU-established taxable person registers directly with the AEDT through the MyGuichet e-government portal, whereas a non-EU entity must appoint an approved Luxembourg VAT representative. A default-transparent SCSp does not file corporate income tax returns in its own name, but still needs a VAT identification number where it carries out an independent economic activity; partners report their allocable share on their own Luxembourg or foreign tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under Article 175 LIR, the SCSp may irrevocably elect to be subject to corporate income tax as a resident corporation, thereby losing fiscal transparency. Hybrid mismatch consequences under the ATAD transposition (Luxembourg law of 21 December 2018) may additionally require the SCSp to be reclassified as transparent or opaque in order to eliminate mismatch outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) — Luxembourg Value Added Tax (Luxembourg VAT Code of 12 February 1979)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (net of VAT) for taxable persons established in Luxembourg under the small-business VAT exemption scheme (Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Code); non-established foreign suppliers have no registration threshold and must register from the first taxable supply made in Luxembourg, subject to the B2B reverse-charge and the OSS/IOSS special schemes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls (CTC), digital stamping, or pre-clearance APIs for B2B invoicing. E-invoicing is permitted under the European standard EN 16931; public-sector invoices flow through the Peppol network, and the MyGuichet/LuxTrust e-delivery infrastructure provides the authenticated digital channel. Mandatory structured B2B e-invoicing will be phased in according to the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) roadmap, with target dates in the 2030–2035 horizon.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: the 0% export rate applies where the transfer of power to dispose of and the dispatch or transport of goods outside the European Union is evidenced, provided the exporter can prove departure from the territory of the Community within 90 days of the time of supply. For services: B2B supplies to a customer established outside Luxembourg or outside the EU are generally outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the customer-location place-of-supply rule, so no zero-rating refinement is required; services directly linked to exported goods may qualify for exemption with credit. In an SCSp ESOP trust context, passive equity holding and plan administration are VAT-neutral where the employer-customer is a B2B recipient established outside Luxembourg; any Luxembourg domestic payroll-related administration services remain taxable at the standard rate unless a specific exemption applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document / ENS) with the EX movement reference and proof of release from the EU customs office
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Commercial invoice, purchase order and contract demonstrating the export supply
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank settlement evidence proving foreign-currency repatriation of the export consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg permits retrospective VAT assessment where export zero-rating documentation is defective: the VAT is clawed back at 17.0% with statutory default interest running from the original due date. Administrative fines under Articles 85–90 of the VAT Code can reach 100% of the VAT at stake; qualified tax fraud carries criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, and the limitation period for fraudulent filings extends to 10 years. AEDT audit practice scrutinises the export document trail, commercial terms, and the economic reality of FX repatriation; substantively unsupported zero-rating claims incur clawback without regard to good faith.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem and under the oversight of the European Central Bank (ECB)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full capital- and current-account convertibility under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the Luxembourg statutory framework on financial relations with foreign countries. The euro is legal tender; no exchange-control or prior-authorisation regime applies to inward or outward capital movements. Profit remittance, capital repayment, and partner distributions of an SCSp are unrestricted for residents and non-residents alike, subject only to valid RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) registration and the bank's AML/KYC clearance. Because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, distributions are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at the entity level; Luxembourg-source income is assessed at the partner level under the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR), and a Luxembourg taxable establishment or permanent representative may trigger corporate income tax and municipal business tax exposure only if the SCSp is deemed to carry on a Luxembourg trade or business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timeline applies to export proceeds in Luxembourg. Export receipts may be retained in any currency, freely converted, or used for offshore settlement. The only obligation is statistical: resident entities must report cross-border payments to the BCL for balance-of-payments purposes where aggregate flows with a single non-resident counterparty exceed EUR 12,500 per calendar month.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Operational Account (EUR/USD/GBP) with a segregated Capital Escrow Sub-Account designated for ESOP share-purchase reserves; dedicated corporate fiduciary desk for special-purpose partnerships
Operational Account with integrated Treasury & Escrow product suite; supports mandate-based remote sign-off where the general partner is a Luxembourg-regulated professional of the financial sector
Operational Current Account with multi-currency overlay and Capital Escrow facility aligned to employee share incentive plan administration

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Domestic Operational Account (EUR); limited appetite for multi-layer SCSp beneficial-ownership chains and USD clearing
Institutional Cash Account with Clearstream Luxembourg and Euroclear connectivity; subject to institutional minimum balances and heightened AML documentation for trust structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility. Luxembourg-authorised EMIs (CSSF-regulated under the Law of 19 December 2016 on e-money institutions) may provide payment accounts but cannot originate commercial letters of credit or provide escrow-grade capital-call custody. Non-Luxembourg digital EMIs passporting under PSD2 (for example Wise Europe, Revolut Business, Velvet) are legally able to service an SCSp, yet most issuer risk departments reject a special-purpose ESOP trust with non-resident beneficiaries and an interposed corporate general partner. Recommended architecture: Tier-1 Luxembourg bank as primary clearing and escrow institution, with a fintech EMI used only for sub-EUR 100,000 employee expense reimbursements or small payroll disbursements via SEPA Instant.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is de facto required for at least one general partner or board signatory at account opening. Remote video KYC is legally permissible under the Law of 25 March 2020 amending the AML Law of 12 November 2004, but Tier-1 Luxembourg banks continue to mandate an in-person interview at the Luxembourg branch for complex partnerships such as an SCSp with non-resident ultimate owners. An alternative is remote onboarding through a CSSF-approved professional of the financial sector introducing the client under a written delegation agreement. Non-resident directors without EU nexus must provide an apostilled power of attorney, certified passport copies, and bank-to-bank reference letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp perceived as a shell or 'mailbox' entity lacking Luxembourg economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (1) executed Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) containing commercial-substance covenants; (2) ESOP Trust Deed and employee share incentive plan rules; (3) employee census, grant schedule, and vesting timeline; (4) Luxembourg registered-office agreement with an approved professional agent; (5) evidence of a Luxembourg-based administrator or payroll service provider; (6) capital-call notices and forward funding projections; (7) independent legal opinion confirming that the trust activity does not constitute MiFID investment business or a reserved banking activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity across the partnership chain (nominee general partner, bearer interests, or tiered ownership)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) full ownership-chain chart terminating in natural persons; (2) active RBE registration certificate recording the nature and extent of each beneficial interest; (3) certified passports of every signatory and each partner holding 25% or more; (4) notarised nominee-elimination declarations or register extracts; (5) up-to-date RCSL (Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register) excerpt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for inbound ESOP capital from a non-EU parent or a multi-layered intermediate holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble: (1) audited financial statements of the parent and immediate remitter; (2) board resolution authorising the ESOP funding and share purchase; (3) bank reference letter from the remitting institution; (4) transfer-pricing and economic-rationale memorandum explaining the ESOP structure; (5) signed indemnity letter in favour of the Luxembourg bank; (6) wire narrative containing 'ESOP Contribution — Share Purchase Reserve' with subscription-agreement reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-routing complexity: account receives equity settlement proceeds and disburses cash to employees resident in multiple foreign jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (1) employee tax-residency and social-security status schedule; (2) ESOP administration agreement with the payroll or third-party service provider; (3) signed ESOP participation agreements and payout terms; (4) confirmation that share settlement will occur via Clearstream Banking Luxembourg or Euroclear book-entry transfer; (5) withholding and social-security calculation memoranda covering Luxembourg income tax, CCSS social security, and foreign tax obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: EUR capital injections route via SWIFT MT103 cleared over T2 (TARGET2 euro RTGS), or via SEPA Credit Transfer when the remitter is EEA-based. The payment order must include beneficiary IBAN and BIC, the exact RCSL-registered legal name, and ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity) or 'INVS' (investment) with the free-text narrative 'Direct Investment — Equity Capital Injection under [capital-call reference]' to satisfy the ECB balance-of-payments purpose classification. USD injections route via SWIFT MT202 COV with a Tier-1 New York correspondent (e.g., BNY Mellon or Citi) together with an MT103 detail record; the remitter must attach the capital-call notice and signed subscription agreement to prevent AML holds. Same-day value applies for TARGET2/SEPA Instant connections; USD settlement occurs T+1 via CHIPS or Fedwire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement uses: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant (sub-EUR 100,000) for EEA employee distributions; (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA payouts and multi-currency vendor settlements; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) with a confirming bank for share purchases from sellers in high-risk jurisdictions, with the cash leg executed via MT103/MT202 in the confirming bank's books; (4) Clearstream Banking Luxembourg and Euroclear Bank book-entry settlement for underlying equity transfers, with the cash leg settled same-day through the SCSp's Tier-1 bank account. Payout narratives must reference 'Exercise/vesting of ESOP units' or 'Settlement of put option' together with the applicable calculation invoice to preserve audit trail integrity under CSSF Circular 19/732.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery FX Forwards (EUR versus USD, GBP, CHF) with maturities up to 12 months, hedging committed ESOP repurchase liabilities; documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement governed by Luxembourg law where the counterparty is a Luxembourg bank, with the SCSp's pass-through status disclosed in the ISDA Schedule and Section 3 representations.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in restricted currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) cash-settled in EUR against the ECB euro foreign-exchange reference rate or the WM/Reuters 4 p.m. London fix; admissible only where the SCSp demonstrates genuine employee equity-repurchase exposure denominated in the restricted currency.

Cross-Currency Swaps combining FX and interest-rate risk for 1-5 year tenors, hedging long-dated ESOP obligations in USD, GBP, or CHF; requires an executed Credit Support Annex (CSA) where collateralised and treasury-committee approval.

FX Swaps exchanging principal and interest between EUR and a foreign currency for temporary reallocation of locked-up share-purchase cash; treated as two linked legs (spot plus forward) and prohibited for speculative leverage.

Vanilla FX Options, including zero-premium collars and participating forwards, strictly limited to employee-repurchase hedging; the SCSp must be categorised by the bank as a professional or eligible counterparty under MiFID II (large-undertaking test requiring two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total above EUR 20 million, net turnover above EUR 40 million, or own funds above EUR 2 million), otherwise a full appropriateness assessment applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the SCSp (confirmation annuelle) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the eJustice portal, including declaration of beneficial owners (immatriculation des bénéficiaires effectifs) if changes occurred.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via eJustice portal; beneficial ownership filing to the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) maintained by LBR.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month of the anniversary of the entity's registration date (date of filing of the articles of association); RBE confirmation must be filed within one month of any change in beneficial ownership and confirmed annually at the same deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty EUR 50 per filing if settled within one month; thereafter increased administrative penalties up to EUR 750 per RCS filing. Persistent failure for the annual confirmation and RBE update may lead to judicial dissolution and strike-off from the RCS, loss of limited liability shield for the general partner, and director disqualification risks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) for SCSp entities meeting minimum size thresholds or where all partners are legal entities; otherwise filing may be required by the underlying fund documentation or by the general partner's own filing obligations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through the eCDF (Electronic Collection of Financial Documents) platform / Luxembourg Business Registers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year (unless consolidated at a parent level and exempt under Luxembourg rules).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 5,000 for non-compliance; publication of the annual accounts is mandatory once filed. Failure to file may block the annual confirmation, trigger criminal fines for the general manager, and expose the entity or partners to administrative dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation (confirmation des bénéficiaires effectifs) for the RBE register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month of the anniversary of registration; additionally, any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years for wilful failure to disclose beneficial ownership; also blocking of the RCS annual confirmation until the RBE declaration is filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: SCSp is exempt from mandatory statutory audit if it qualifies as a small undertaking and none of its partners is a legal entity; audit is compulsory if the SCSp exceeds any two of three thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average employees 50, or if it forms part of a group requiring consolidated audit. Investment fund vehicles under CSSF supervision or with an AIFM may require a statutory audit irrespective of size thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements prepared under Luxembourg GAAP (law of 19 December 2002, as amended) or IFRS as adopted by the EU if the entity elects or is required by its constitutive documents or group policy.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Luxembourg law, the SCSp must keep an updated register of beneficial owners at its registered office. A confirmation must be filed annually with the RBE confirming that the information on file remains accurate, with any changes reported within one month of occurrence. The SCSp must disclose its RBE status and file reference to the general partner and to the RCS upon annual confirmation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 15,000 per annum for small-to-mid SCSp, depending on CSSF or investor requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) applies at the headline rate of 17.00% for the 2024 tax year, composed of a 15.00% national corporate income tax rate plus a 7.00% solidarity surcharge (contribution au fonds de l'emploi) levied on the base corporate income tax, resulting in an aggregate CIT rate of 16.05% before municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal). Subject to collective bargaining and territorial allocation, the effective aggregate statutory burden in Luxembourg City (municipal business tax rate of 6.75%) reaches approximately 24.94%. For SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) entities classified as transparent, profits are generally attributed directly to partners, and the SCSp itself is not subject to CIT. No statutory tax holiday regime applies to employee stock ownership trust vehicles; however, the IP box regime (80% exemption for qualifying intellectual property income) and participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividend and capital gains income) remain available at the level of corporate partners, provided the holding and substance requirements are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax return form Model 1 (for ordinary trading companies; the SCSp as tax-transparent entity generally does not file a standalone CIT return) and partner-level model forms 100/101, filed electronically via the Luxembourg tax authority e-filing platform 'MyGuichet' (guichet.lu) or the dedicated professional e-filing portal of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed by 30 June of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end. For fiscal years ending on a date other than 31 December, the return is due within six months after the close of the fiscal year. Extended deadlines may be granted upon written request to the ACD, but such extension is discretionary and limited in practice to 31 December of the filing year. Where the SCSp is fiscally transparent, each partner must include its allocable share of SCSp income in its own Luxembourg income tax return; non-resident corporate partners with a Luxembourg permanent establishment arising from the SCSp activity must file a separate Luxembourg branch tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the taxpayer: name, legal form (SCSp), RCS registration number, and fiscal number (numéro d'identification, NIF).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must indicate their foreign tax identification number (TIN) and, if applicable, the Luxembourg permanent establishment number assigned by the ACD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of profit or loss: domestic source income, foreign source income, deductible expenses, and net taxable results attributed to the reporting partner before specific deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must declare only the profits attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment or to Luxembourg-source income derived through the SCSp.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from shareholding, dividends, and participation exemption (régime des sociétés mères et filiales) claimed at the level of a corporate partner holding the SCSp interests.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Corporate partners applying the participation exemption must attach evidence of the qualifying shareholding duration, the minimum percentage/taxable threshold, and a declaration that the income is not deducted by a subsidiary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward computation; previous tax losses available for set-off against current taxable income with a five-year carryforward window only (loss carryback is disallowed).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners cannot carry Luxembourg losses into a foreign tax return but may carry the loss at the level of the Luxembourg permanent establishment; no cross-border migration of the carryforward remains available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of withholding taxes on Luxembourg-source income, including dividend withholding tax, interest withholding tax, and royalty withholding tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must identify treaty-protected rates and attach the relevant double tax treaty and tax residence certificate (form 360/361 or OECD TRC) for relief at source or via reclaim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax reporting (impôt sur la fortune) if the SCSp has opted for corporate taxation or if a corporate partner is itself subject to net wealth tax on its Luxembourg assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners are generally not subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax on SCSp assets absent a Luxembourg permanent establishment; where a PE exists, reporting occurs on the PE's wealth tax schedule at 0.50% of net allocable assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of a Luxembourg CIT return triggers a 'taxation d'office' (automatic assessment) and a penalty of up to EUR 1,000 per return, plus monthly delay interest of 0.8% on taxes due. For failure to file altogether, the ACD may impose a minimum penalty of EUR 250 and additional late payment interest at 0.8% per month. Where gross negligence or deliberate concealment is proven, a surcharge of up to 25% of the underpaid tax applies, and criminal penalties of imprisonment (up to 8 days to 5 years) and fines up to EUR 10,000 may be imposed for fraudulent conduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax rate is 15% (applicable to distributions made by Luxembourg capital companies). The SCSp, as a transparent partnership, is not legally a withholding agent for dividends; distributions or allocations by the SCSp to its partners are generally treated as partnership profit allocations rather than dividend distributions at the Luxembourg source level. However, where an SCSp is beneficially owned by a Luxembourg capital company that later distributes income to its shareholders, the standard 15% dividend withholding tax applies, reduced by the participation exemption in qualifying intra-group situations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double tax treaty reduction of dividend, interest, or royalty withholding tax, the beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a Luxembourg tax residence certificate (form 360/361 or the OECD-recommended template) from the ACD certifying fiscal residence in the treaty jurisdiction; (2) submit a written Treaty Relief at Source (TRAS) application to the Luxembourg withholding agent prior to the payment, or file a reclaim for excess withholding within the statute of limitations (5 years); and (3) maintain evidence of beneficial ownership, the shareholding period (for the participation exemption: 10% or acquisition cost of at least EUR 1.2 million held without interruption for 12 months in case of liquidation, or the standard holding period), and compliance with anti-abuse substance requirements under the Principal Purpose Test. The Luxembourg-Australia DTA is not applicable to an Australian-resident partner absent specific treaty provisions; where no treaty exists, domestic Luxembourg rates apply. The ACD automatic exchange and domestic anti-abuse rules require that any treaty relief must not be the primary purpose of the arrangement; the partner must demonstrate that the SCSp is a genuine establishment with adequate personnel, premises, and economic activity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on outbound interest payments under domestic law (except for certain interest payments treated as 'artificial' arrangements covered by AEOI). Outbound royalty withholding tax is 0% under domestic Luxembourg law as from 1 January 2018 for royalties on copyrighted software, patents, trademarks, know-how, and similar intellectual property, provided the anti-abuse conditions are met, including the requirement that the royalty income is subject to tax in the hands of the beneficial owner. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may further reduce such withholding tax to 0% between associated companies; where treaty protection is sought, the relevant DTA (e.g., with France, Germany, Belgium) typically fixes dividend WHT at 5% to 15%, interest and royalty WHT at 0% to 10%, subject to the Principal Purpose Test and the substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg does not prescribe a fixed statutory monetary threshold for mandatory Local File or Master File preparation; the obligation follows the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and the EU Transfer Pricing Directive (EU) 2022/2523. In practice, Luxembourg taxpayers engaged in cross-border related-party transactions or achieving revenues exceeding EUR 50 million, or intra-group services and financing exceeding EUR 10 million, are expected to keep contemporaneous documentation consistent with the ACD's documentation requirements. The Luxembourg tax authorities apply a risk-based approach and require the local file for controlled transactions above EUR 1 million in aggregate. An SCSp operating as an employee stock ownership trust must document its intercompany transactions (e.g., allocation of directors' fees, equity transfer pricing, management fees, and financing arrangements) at arm's length even in the absence of a statutory threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Given the SCSp's character as a tax-transparent special limited partnership, economic substance requirements are not imposed by the Luxembourg Civil Code for the SCSp itself, but Luxembourg tax law and the OECD/G20 Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) Inclusive Framework, as implemented through the Multilateral Instrument (MLI) and the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD), require that any arrangement not be artificial. Since the target scope is an employee stock ownership trust (ESOP), the trust-like vehicle must avoid classification as a 'shell' under the EU's Directive (EU) 2016/1164 (ATAD) anti-abuse provisions; local substance is evidenced by the existence of a Luxembourg-registered service provider (domiciliation agent), a Luxembourg-based accountant and tax filer, the maintenance of minute books, the physical presence of a local board of managers (managing partner), and the performance of genuine decision-making functions. Where the SCSp is treated as a tax-transparent entity, the 'economic substance' assessment is conducted at the partner level; a partner that is a pure conduit in a low-tax jurisdiction without effective staff and activity will fail the Principal Purpose Test and may be denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of income allocations from the SCSp on the partner's Luxembourg tax return, or the artificial shifting of profits to a tax-haven partner without commercial substance, including failure to file the tax return for more than two consecutive years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 73 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), tax evasion carries a fine of up to EUR 10,000 and imprisonment of 8 days to 6 months (or one year for repeated offenses). Fraudulent claims for exemption or treaty relief trigger a 25% surcharge on evaded tax, plus late interest at 0.8% per month from the due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing partner (gérant) of an SCSp may be held personally liable under Luxembourg civil law for the tax debts of the partnership if they act in flagrant disregard of corporate interests or use the partnership as a mere sham (simulation). Luxembourg courts allow 'piercing of the corporate veil' where the partnership is used to evade tax, resulting in joint and several liability for unpaid corporate tax and net wealth tax, plus damages for fiscal negligence. In egregious criminal cases, the managing partner may be subject to a personal arrest warrant, travel ban, or imprisonment, and the ACD may seize personal assets of the director to satisfy the partnership's liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of an SCSp with no employees, no premises, no real business purpose, and no active administration of an employee stock ownership plan, solely to obtain Luxembourg treaty benefits or to defer income allocation to beneficiaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg's abuse-of-law doctrine (article 6 of the General Tax Law) and the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI, the ACD will deny treaty benefits and recharacterize the structure as wholly taxable at the Luxembourg entity level, imposing corporate income tax at 17.00% (effective up to 24.94%), a 5% late-filing surcharge, and net wealth tax of 0.50%. A 'shell entity' status additionally triggers disqualification from the EU Interest and Royalties Directive and the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, exposing the full income to withholding taxes and interest penalties up to 25% of the tax due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant or corporate services provider that knowingly establishes a sham SCSp may be personally liable for all resulting tax arrears, penalties, and interest under the legal concept of 'faute détachable' (separate fault). Administrative seizure of assets and a commercial ban (interdiction de gérer) may be imposed for up to 10 years. Criminal sanctions for forgery of substance documentation include a fine of EUR 8,000 to EUR 100,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years (Ordre des avocats et des conseils; Luxembourg Criminal Code article 196).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify the beneficial owner of the employee stock ownership trust, failure to report suspicious transactions arising from stock option financing, or the use of the SCSp to conceal the transfer of corporate control without proper AML registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 on AML/FTF and the amended law of 27 January 2020, any professional of the financial sector or trust/company service provider (TCSP) that fails to conduct customer due diligence, or fails to report suspicious transactions, is subject to an administrative fine of up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover (for legal persons), and the SCSp may be subject to a forced dissolution order by the Luxembourg Public Prosecutor's Office. Criminal penalties range from EUR 1,000 to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years, depending on the severity of the breach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managing partners of a TCSP or the SCSp itself who knowingly facilitate ML/FT activity face imprisonment of 5 to 10 years (Criminal Code article 506-3) and fines up to EUR 500,000. Personal travel bans and asset freezes may be ordered by the Luxembourg courts pending investigation. Liability is joint and several for the full amounts laundered through the SCSp, including disgorgement of profits, and the director may be permanently barred from serving as director in any Luxembourg entity (removal from the 21-day commercial register).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Maintain Transfer Pricing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's length financing terms for employee stock purchase loans, excessive management fees charged by the SCSp to the parent company, or the absence of contemporaneous TP documentation for intercompany equity transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg's TP documentation penalty is governed by article 35 of the Luxembourg income tax law; failure to produce documentation upon ACD request triggers an estimated assessment at the ACD's discretion plus a monetary penalty of up to EUR 10,000, and a surcharge of 25% of the tax avoided where the TP adjustment is accepted. For SCSp structures, profit recharacterization may lead to full taxation of the trustee's fees and stock-option benefits at the corporate partner level.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify inaccurate TP documentation without due diligence are subject to civil restitution claims from the participating affiliates, joint liability for the corporate tax shortfall, and for severe intentional distortions (e.g., fake invoices from a shell service provider), criminal conviction for fraud and forgery under Luxembourg Criminal Code article 196 and article 210, with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 100,000.
